newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Junk softer, new deals mixed.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Junk softer, new deals mixed.

text.p: U.S. high-yield issuance continued at a heated pace on Tuesday with nearly $1.5 billion priced, but the market softened, dealers and buysiders said.

Tight pricings and the sheer number of issues prevented the powerful gains seen for new issues so often in the past month, they said, not to mention lackluster trade in the underlying U.S. Treasury arena. But activity remained quiet making a judgement against the market difficult, traders said.
In any event, issues priced on Tuesday were seen trading both slightly stronger and slightly weaker than original levels, they said.

Outdoor Systems $500 million B1/B rated 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced to yield nine percent via CIBC Wood Gundy, were quoted down about 1/2 point at 98-1/2 bid, 98-3/4 offer, traders said.
Short covering on the issue late in the session gave its price some buoyancy, said one trader.

Elsewhere, Big Flower Press's $250 million B2/B rated 10-year senior subordinated notes also closed with bids about 1/2 point lower with the broad market at 98-1/2. The notes were priced to yield nine percent by a BT Securities Corp, Credit Suisse First Boston and Goldman Sachs syndicate.
On the buyside, some fund managers said the historical tightness of spreads has kept them from buying new issues altogether. Some degree of price correction is in the cards, they contended.

"I think a lot of deals have begun to push the envelope on spread," said Jerry Paul, manager of INVESCO's High-Yield and Select Income funds. "There are plenty of deals to get done and that will take a little bit of the stuffing out of the marketplace, though nothing severe."
Paul also warned that some "marginal credits" are starting to show up in greater numbers.
Looking ahead, high-yield telecommunication and satellite deals have captured attentions, including the recently restructured offering from Chase Telecommunications.

The deal, originally billed as a zero coupon offering, on Monday was upped in size and given a three-year prefunded structure, sources said. Price talk was adjusted from 14 percent with 15 to 17 percent equity to a 13-1/2 percent coupon with 20 percent equity, they added.
One trader not involved in the deal said the demise of the zeros may not be a strike against the particular structure.

"If I'm an investor and if I can get a cash pay or a zero, I might just want the cash pay," one trader said. "If that's coming to market amidst a whole bunch of cash pays that could have impacted it. It's more a matter of timing."

Turning to investment grades, traders called spreads firm to marginally weaker against Treasuries in quiet dealings. Despite a large forward calendar, supply on Tuesday was limited with a $150 million offering of five-year floating rate debentures from Consolidated Edison of New York.
A $1.0 billion AAA-rated global from Bayerische Landesbank and a $500 million A1/A-plus rated global from American Express are expected to price as early as Wednesday.
And Young Broadcasting's $200 million B2/B 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced by Merrill Lynch & Co Inc to yield 8.89 percent, were seen offered down about 1/2 at 98-1/2.

Despite the downtrades and a broadly weaker secondary market, dealers were reluctant to mark an end to heady positive sentiments enjoyed for two months now. They did concede, however, that buysiders are able to "cherry pick for the lowest fruit on the tree."
"It's slow and if there was a select one or two issues volume might have picked up, but there's a lot out there to read right now," said one trader at a large New York shop.
